{"parentUuid":"5b7e1465-5814-4e08-86bc-1cfaed2d044e","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0620594e-4d98-4377-a0b2-f29d0c1d1779","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017sd7KXicDmrw9V6ViyGWL4","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Data Bites in the admin console. Any signed-in user may do everything here,\nchart images and Site previews included, except delete, which is Director\nonly.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Mapping\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, File, Form, HTTPException, Request, UploadFile\nfrom fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import chart_images, data_bites, editor, public_site\nfrom app.flash import SITE_NOTE, confirm\nfrom app.auth import current_user, require_csrf, require_director\nfrom app.content import STATUS_LABELS, ContentError\nfrom app.rendering import images_without_description\nfrom app.routes import editing\nfrom app.routes.site_preview import site_file\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin/data-bites\", dependencies=[Depends(current_user)])\n_MAX_IMAGE_MB = chart_images.MAX_BYTES // chart_images.MIB\n\n\ndef _site_preview(request: Request, form: Mapping[str, str], bite: sqlite3.Row | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The Site preview of `form`'s edits to `bite` (None for a new Data\n    Bite), as HTML, served from the preview's copy of the site.\"\"\"\n    at = (request.app.url_path_for(\"bite_preview_site\", bite_id=bite[\"id\"], path=\"\")\n          if bite is not None else request.app.url_path_for(\"new_bite_preview_site\", path=\"\"))\n    return public_site.data_bite_preview(form, bite).render_preview(str(at))\n\n\ndef _images(request: Request, bite_id: int) -> editor.ImageLinks:\n    return editing.image_links(request, \"serve_image\", bite_id=bite_id)\n\n\ndef _list_page(request: Request, user: sqlite3.Row, *, error: str | None = None,\n               form: dict | None = None, status_code: int = 200):\n    form = form or {\"title\": \"\", \"slug\": \"\", \"body\": \"\"}\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/data_bites.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Data Bites\", \"home_path\": \"/admin\", \"user\": user,\n         \"bites\": data_bites.list_all(), \"status_labels\": STATUS_LABELS,\n         \"error\": error, \"form\": form,\n         \"editor_html\": editor.editor_html(form[\"body\"], \"\", None),\n         \"site_preview\": _site_preview(\n             request, {**form, \"body\": editor.full_body(form[\"body\"], \"\")}, None),\n         \"preview_path\": request.app.url_path_for(\"preview_new_bite\")},\n        status_code=status_code,\n    )\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\ndef list_bites(request: Request, user=Depends(current_user)):\n    return _list_page(request, user)\n\n\n@router.post(\"\", dependencies=[Depends(require_csrf)])\ndef create_bite(request: Request, user=Depends(current_user), title: str = Form(\"\"),\n                slug: str = Form(\"\"), posted: editor.Posted = Depends(editing.posted)):\n    try:\n        data_bites.create(title, slug, editor.saved_body(posted, None, None), user[\"id\"])\n    except ContentError as exc:\n        return _list_page(request, user, error=str(exc), status_code=400,\n                          form=editor.form_after(posted, title, slug, \"\", None, None))\n    confirm(request, \"Data Bite created as a Draft.\")\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/data-bites\", status_code=303)\n\n\n# A new Data Bite's Site preview. Before the /{bite_id} routes, which would\n# otherwise take \"preview\" for an id.\n\n@router.post(\"/preview\", dependencies=[Depends(require_csrf)])\ndef preview_new_bite(request: Request, title: str = Form(\"\"),\n                     posted: editor.Posted = Depends(editing.posted)):\n    \"\"\"The create form's Site preview, for its frame and \"Preview on site\".\n    Saves nothing.\"\"\"\n    shown = editing.previewed(posted, None, None)\n    return HTMLResponse(_site_preview(request, {\"title\": title, \"body\": shown}, None))\n\n\n@router.get(\"/preview/{path:path}\")\ndef new_bite_preview_site(path: str):\n    \"\"\"The create form's Site preview's copy of the site: only its stylesheet,\n    as a new Data Bite has no chart images (app.routes.site_preview).\"\"\"\n    return site_file(path, images={})\n\n\ndef _edit_page(request: Request, user: sqlite3.Row, bite: sqlite3.Row, *,\n               error: str | None = None, form: dict | None = None,\n               status_code: int = 200):\n    form = form or editor.form_for(bite)\n    # The body with its locked blocks, which only the server sees.\n    body = editor.full_body(form[\"body\"], bite[\"body\"])\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/data_bite_edit.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Edit Data Bite\", \"home_path\": \"/admin\", \"user\": user,\n         \"bite\": bite, \"status_labels\": STATUS_LABELS,\n         \"error\": error, \"form\": form,\n         \"editor_html\": editor.editor_html(form[\"body\"], bite[\"body\"],\n                                           _images(request, bite[\"id\"]).src),\n         \"images\": list(data_bites.images(bite[\"id\"])),\n         \"site_preview\": _site_preview(request, {**form, \"body\": body}, bite),\n         \"preview_path\": request.app.url_path_for(\"preview_bite\", bite_id=bite[\"id\"]),\n         \"undescribed_images\": images_without_description(body),\n         \"max_image_mb\": _MAX_IMAGE_MB,\n         \"max_images\": chart_images.MAX_PER_ITEM},\n        status_code=status_code,\n    )\n\n\ndef _get_or_404(bite_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    bite = data_bites.get(bite_id)\n    if bite is None:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404)\n    return bite\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{bite_id}\")\ndef edit_bite_form(request: Request, bite_id: int, user=Depends(current_user)):\n    return _edit_page(request, user, _get_or_404(bite_id))\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{bite_id}\", dependencies=[Depends(require_csrf)])\ndef edit_bite(request: Request, bite_id: int, user=Depends(current_user),\n              title: str = Form(\"\"), slug: str = Form(\"\"),\n              posted: editor.Posted = Depends(editing.posted), item_base: str = Form(\"\")):\n    bite = _get_or_404(bite_id)\n    image_name = _images(request, bite_id).name\n    try:\n        data_bites.update(bite_id, title, slug,\n                          editor.saved_edit(posted, bite, item_base, image_name),\n                          base=item_base or None)\n    except ContentError as exc:\n        # Shown over the item as stored now, which a stale form missed.\n        current = _get_or_404(bite_id)\n        return _edit_page(request, user, current, error=str(exc),\n                          status_code=editing.refused_status(exc),\n                          form=editor.form_after(posted, title, slug, item_base,\n                                                 current[\"body\"], image_name))\n    confirm(request, \"Data Bite saved.\")\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/data-bites/{bite_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{bite_id}/preview\", dependencies=[Depends(require_csrf)])\ndef preview_bite(request: Request, bite_id: int, title: str = Form(\"\"),\n                 posted: editor.Posted = Depends(editing.posted)):\n    \"\"\"The edit form's Site preview, of its unsaved title and body, for its\n    frame and \"Preview on site\". Saves nothing.\"\"\"\n    bite = _get_or_404(bite_id)\n    shown = editing.previewed(posted, bite[\"body\"],\n                      _images(request, bite_id).name)\n    return HTMLResponse(_site_preview(request, {\"title\": title, \"body\": shown}, bite))\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{bite_id}/preview/{path:path}\")\ndef bite_preview_site(bite_id: int, path: str):\n    \"\"\"The Site preview's copy of the site: its stylesheet and the Data\n    Bite's chart images, draft or not (app.routes.site_preview).\"\"\"\n    return site_file(path, images=public_site.data_bite_files(_get_or_404(bite_id)))\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{bite_id}/images/{name}\")\ndef serve_image(bite_id: int, name: str):\n    path = data_bites.images(bite_id).get(name)\n    if path is None:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404)\n    return chart_images.response(path)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{bite_id}/images\", dependencies=[Depends(require_csrf)])\ndef upload_image(request: Request, bite_id: int, user=Depends(current_user),\n                 file: UploadFile | None = File(None)):\n    bite = _get_or_404(bite_id)\n    try:\n        if not data_bites.add_image(bite_id, chart_images.read(file)):\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=404)\n    except ContentError as exc:\n        return _edit_page(request, user, bite, accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. GitHub Pages serves static files\nonly: it cannot run Python and has no database. Students have two weeks and no\nhosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\nattractive target the moment it is public.\n\n## Decision\n\nThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\nis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\nis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). A\n`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\nis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\nis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). A Site preview's links are relative\nand resolve there (app.public_site.Page.render_preview).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi import HTTPException\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse, Response\n\nfrom app import chart_images\nfrom app.routes.public import pdf_response, stylesheet\n\n# A path in the site, as the *_path functions of app.public_site make them:\n# never starting with \"/\" or a backslash, so a redirect to \"/\" + it stays on\n# this site.\n_SITE_PATH = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(?:/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)*\", re.ASCII)\n\n\ndef site_file(path: str, images: dict[str, Path], pdfs: dict[str, Path] | None = None) -> Response:\n    \"\"\"What a Site preview's link to `path` in the site gets: the stylesheet,\n    or one of the previewed item's own chart `images` or `pdfs` (a Report's\n    file), by path in the site, which the public site would not serve for a\n    draft. Any other page sends the browser to the published one.\"\"\"\n    if path == \"style.css\":\n        return stylesheet()\n    if path in images:\n        return chart_images.response(images[path])\n    if pdfs and path in pdfs:\n        return pdf_response(pdfs[path])\n    if not _SITE_PATH.fullmatch(path):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/\" + path, status_code=303)","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"serverClassifierContext":{"request":"2fdceb46-0297-475f-b03b-6d44711507b9","context":{"git_state":{"cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","root":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","branch":"main","default_branch":"main","status":{"clean":false,"counts":{"staged":0,"modified":1,"untracked":null,"untracked_normal":4},"porcelain":null,"truncated":false},"visibility":{"origin":{"host":"github.com","remote":"DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"},"push_remote":"origin","remotes":[{"name":"origin","host":"github.com","remote":"DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}],"visibility_cache":[{"host":"github.com","remote":"DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}]}},"live_cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","platform":"macos"}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0c29839c-a7e6-4b2d-b856-6041c6405cb1","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"5f1453e3-22ca-48ab-bcdf-08e3c322f1be","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"07964d4d-fb88-4d0d-8fdd-580a4601033a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaL8L1eZMYHDzfjFj9RV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've read T14 (#17), the spec (#14), CONTEXT.md, and the code T14 touches. T14 has 13 acceptance criteria, so under your global CLAUDE.md rule here's the numbered plan. I'll wait for your approval before starting.\n\n**Plan for T14**\n\n1. **Refs and tombstones** (`app/db.py`, `app/content.py`, new `app/site_links.py`)\n   - Add a `ref` column to both tables through `ADDED_COLUMNS`. `init_db` backfills it and creates a unique index on each table.\n   - A trigger stops a ref from ever changing.\n   - A new `deleted_refs(kind, ref, deleted_at)` table.\n   - `ContentTable.create` picks a ref inside a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. It checks the ref against both tables and `deleted_refs`, tries again on a collision, and raises after 3 attempts.\n   - `delete` writes the tombstone in the same transaction as the delete.\n   - Tests first: backfill, uniqueness, ref unchanged by edits, tombstoned-ref retry, failure after 3 attempts.\n2. **Render pipeline** (`app/rendering.py`)\n   - nh3 runs its URL-scheme check before its attribute filter (I checked this). So I let the `https`, `mailto`, `image`, `report` and `data-bite` schemes through, and resolve every one in the attribute filter:\n     - `a href` survives only as `https:`, `mailto:`, or a site reference that resolves.\n     - `img src` survives only as `image:<name>`.\n   - A small `html.parser` pass on nh3's output then unwraps each `<a>` left without an href and drops each `<img>` left without a src.\n   - This covers raw HTML typed into the Markdown fallback as well as Markdown links.\n3. **Public site, export and Site preview** (`app/public_site.py`)\n   - Each page resolves `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` to `root` plus the target's published path.\n   - The Site preview also resolves the item it shows, since that item is treated \"as if published\".\n   - Update the T10 \"other image URLs\" test.\n4. **Editor server side** (`app/editor.py`, `app/markdown_form.py`)\n   - Site-reference links count as supported, so they aren't locked, and they survive the HTML-to-Markdown step.\n   - The edit and create pages carry the picker's items (title, kind, draft or not). They also carry the state of each unresolvable reference in the body: unpublished, deleted, or unknown.\n5. **Editor script** (`static/editor.js`)\n   - The link panel gets two choices: \"A page on this site\" (a `<select>` of Reports and Data Bites, drafts marked) and \"A web address\" (`https:` or `mailto:` only, anything else refused with a message).\n   - Links that won't resolve are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\", \"Item deleted\", or \"Unknown link\". The marker is a `data-` attribute plus CSS `::after` text, so it is never saved into the body.\n6. **Delete lists what links to the item**\n   - The list page's Delete button (Director only) opens a confirmation page. It lists the items whose bodies link to this one, with a final Delete button.\n   - The existing POST route stays as it is.\n7. **Docs and crawler**\n   - Change the hard rule in CLAUDE.md and add a matching note to ADR-001.\n   - `crawl()` skips `https:` and `mailto:` `<a href>`s. It still fails on root-absolute paths, any other `://` URL, and any `src` that isn't relative.\n   - A test injects a bad URL and shows the crawler fails.\n8. **Finish**\n   - Run the full suite, then `/code-review`, and post its findings on #17.\n   - Do the browser check in Chrome (picker, external-link refusal, the three markers) with screenshots.\n   - Commit at checkpoints (after steps 1–3 and 4–6), with the `T14:` prefix and `Closes #17`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1684,"cache_read_input_tokens":134369,"output_tokens":1886,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":263},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1684,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1886,"cache_read_input_tokens":134369,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1684,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1684},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"bc3712da-0400-4f9a-a043-8fed96ab5f98","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfaL8KYcumaSvNfopB4MK","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:implement","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"6426af30-3199-46ab-81ba-305d3e555685","timestamp":"2026-09-30T21:26:06.259Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"5f1453e3-22ca-48ab-bcdf-08e3c322f1be","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"dce07774-8398-4088-a7f1-6128327aa74d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0620594e-4d98-4377-a0b2-f29d0c1d1779","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"ca4c8f96-dc68-4c20-9f61-84921f322ed0","timestamp":"2026-09-30T21:26:42.897Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01ABsLVUizWcP44DcWT28zA7","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"5f1453e3-22ca-48ab-bcdf-08e3c322f1be","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"d59cba68-aabf-4d07-bfa8-5c8c07bd6ed0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaLCfJ886K96syEUCJFu","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01AbCXCizW6pgHLdhqWkThsM","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t14_refs.py","content":"\"\"\"T14: every Data Bite and Report has an immutable, never-reused `ref`\n(issue #17), which a site link names it by: `report:<ref>` or\n`data-bite:<ref>`.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app import data_bites, db, reports, settings, site_links, users\n\nHEX_REF = re.compile(r\"[0-9a-f]{32}\")\nKINDS = [pytest.param(data_bites, \"data-bite\", id=\"data-bite\"),\n         pytest.param(reports, \"report\", id=\"report\")]\n\n\ndef author() -> int:\n    return users.get_by_email(\"admin@example.test\")[\"id\"]\n\n\ndef create(module, slug: str = \"fall-enrollment\", title: str = \"Fall enrollment\") -> int:\n    return module.create(title, slug, \"Body.\", author())\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"module, kind\", KINDS)\ndef test_a_new_item_gets_a_ref_that_editing_never_changes(module, kind):\n    item_id = create(module)\n    ref = module.get(item_id)[\"ref\"]\n    assert HEX_REF.fullmatch(ref)\n\n    director = users.get_by_email(\"admin@example.test\")\n    edit = {\"user\": director} if module is reports else {}\n    assert module.update(item_id, \"Renamed\", \"renamed\", \"New body.\", **edit)\n    module.set_status(item_id, \"published\")\n    assert module.get(item_id)[\"ref\"] == ref\n    assert site_links.state(f\"{kind}:{ref}\") == \"published\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"module, kind\", KINDS)\ndef test_a_ref_can_never_be_changed_in_the_database(module, kind):\n    item_id = create(module)\n    with pytest.raises(sqlite3.IntegrityError), db.connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(f\"UPDATE {module._TABLE.table} SET ref = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n                     (\"0\" * 32, item_id))\n\n\ndef test_refs_are_unique_across_both_tables():\n    refs = {data_bites.get(create(data_bites, f\"b{n}\"))[\"ref\"] for n in range(5)}\n    refs |= {reports.get(create(reports, f\"r{n}\"))[\"ref\"] for n in range(5)}\n    assert len(refs) == 10\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"module, kind\", KINDS)\ndef test_deleting_an_item_tombstones_its_ref(module, kind):\n    item_id = create(module)\n    reference = f\"{kind}:{module.get(item_id)['ref']}\"\n    assert site_links.state(reference) == \"draft\"\n\n    assert module.delete(item_id)\n    assert site_links.state(reference) == \"deleted\"\n    assert site_links.state(f\"{kind}:{'f' * 32}\") == \"unknown\"\n\n\ndef test_a_ref_names_one_kind_only():\n    ref = reports.get(create(reports))[\"ref\"]\n    assert site_links.state(f\"data-bite:{ref}\") == \"unknown\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"module, kind\", KINDS)\ndef test_a_new_ref_is_never_a_tombstoned_one(module, kind, monkeypatch):\n    \"\"\"The generator is forced to give a deleted item's ref first: the insert\n    tries again, with a fresh one.\"\"\"\n    old = create(module)\n    tombstoned = module.get(old)[\"ref\"]\n    module.delete(old)\n\n    fresh = iter([tombstoned, \"a\" * 32])\n    calls = []\n    monkeypatch.setattr(site_links, \"_generate\",\n                        lambda: calls.append(1) or next(fresh))\n    new = create(module)\n    assert module.get(new)[\"ref\"] == \"a\" * 32\n    assert len(calls) == 2\n    # SQLite may have reused the id; the ref still says \"deleted\".\n    assert site_links.state(f\"{kind}:{tombstoned}\") == \"deleted\"\n\n\ndef test_a_new_ref_is_never_one_the_other_table_uses(monkeypatch):\n    taken = reports.get(create(reports))[\"ref\"]\n    fresh = iter([taken, \"b\" * 32])\n    monkeypatch.setattr(site_links, \"_generate\", lambda: next(fresh))\n    assert data_bites.get(create(data_bites))[\"ref\"] == \"b\" * 32\n\n\ndef test_three_collisions_fail_loudly_and_write_nothing(monkeypatch):\n    taken = reports.get(create(reports))[\"ref\"]\n    monkeypatch.setattr(site_links, \"_generate\", lambda: taken)\n    with pytest.raises(site_links.RefCollision):\n        create(data_bites)\n    assert data_bites.list_all() == []\n\n\nOLD_SCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    name TEXT NOT NULL, role TEXT NOT NULL, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    is_active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')));\nCREATE TABLE data_bites (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    body TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft', author_id INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')));\nCREATE TABLE reports (id re\nimport sqlite3\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app import data_bites, db, reports, settings, site_links, users\n\nHEX_REF = re.compile(r\"[0-9a-f]{32}\")\nKINDS = [pytest.param(data_bites, \"data-bite\", id=\"data-bite\"),\n         pytest.param(reports, \"report\", id=\"report\")]\n\n\ndef author() -> int:\n    return users.get_by_email(\"admin@example.test\")[\"id\"]\n\n\ndef create(module, slug: str = \"fall-enrollment\", title: str = \"Fall enrollment\") -> int:\n    return module.create(title, slug, \"Body.\", author())\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"module, kind\", KINDS)\ndef test_a_new_item_gets_a_ref_that_editing_never_changes(module, kind):\n    item_id = create(module)\n    ref = module.get(item_id)[\"ref\"]\n    assert HEX_REF.fullmatch(ref)\n\n    director = users.get_by_email(\"admin@example.test\")\n    edit = {\"user\": director} if module is reports else {}\n    assert module.update(item_id, \"Renamed\", \"renamed\", \"New body.\", **edit)\n    module.set_status(item_id, \"published\")\n    assert module.get(item_id)[\"ref\"] == ref\n    assert site_links.state(f\"{kind}:{ref}\") == \"published\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"module, kind\", KINDS)\ndef test_a_ref_can_never_be_changed_in_the_database(module, kind):\n    item_id = create(module)\n    with pytest.raises(sqlite3.IntegrityError), db.connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(f\"UPDATE {module._TABLE.table} SET ref = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n                     (\"0\" * 32, item_id))\n\n\ndef test_refs_are_unique_across_both_tables():\n    refs = {data_bites.get(create(data_bites, f\"b{n}\"))[\"ref\"] for n in range(5)}\n    refs |= {reports.get(create(reports, f\"r{n}\"))[\"ref\"] for n in range(5)}\n    assert len(refs) == 10\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"module, kind\", KINDS)\ndef test_deleting_an_item_tombstones_its_ref(module, kind):\n    item_id = create(module)\n    reference = f\"{kind}:{module.get(item_id)['ref']}\"\n    assert site_links.state(reference) == \"draft\"\n\n Built after ADDED_COLUMNS, which may add\n# the column: a unique index, and a trigger that keeps a ref from changing\n# once set.\n_REF_TABLES = (\"data_bites\", \"reports\")\n_REF_RULES = \"\"\"\nCREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS {table}_ref ON {table} (ref);\nCREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {table}_ref_fixed BEFORE UPDATE OF ref ON {table}\n    WHEN OLD.ref IS NOT NULL AND NEW.ref IS NOT OLD.ref\n    BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'a ref never changes'); END;\n\"\"\"\n''')\ns=s.replace('''def init_db() -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        for table, column, definition in ADDED_COLUMNS:\n            existing = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\n            if column not in existing:\n                conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}\")\n''','''def init_db() -> None:\n    # Imported here: app.site_links reads the database through this module.\n    from app import site_links\n\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        for table, column, definition in ADDED_COLUMNS:\n            existing = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\n            if column not in existing:\n                conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}\")\n        for table in _REF_TABLES:\n            conn.executescript(_REF_RULES.format(table=table))\n            # Rows made before refs existed get one now.\n            for (row_id,) in conn.execute(\n                    f\"SELECT id FROM {table} WHERE ref IS NULL\").fetchall():\n                conn.execute(f\"UPDATE {table} SET ref = ? {"parentUuid":"5f02327a-6965-4962-80f5-6ba4529f5196","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaLGVztmHedDQTshHkqi","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01USZS9Noth5wf8r8QfS6UQw","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/site_links.py","content":"\"\"\"Site links: a link in a body to another Data Bite or Report (spec #14,\n\"Links\").\n\nA link names its target by a *site reference*, `data-bite:<ref>` or\n`report:<ref>`, never by title, slug, or id: a title or slug may be edited,\nand SQLite may give a deleted item's id to a new one. Each item's `ref` is 32\nrandom hex characters, set when it is created and never changed (a trigger in\napp.db enforces it) or reused: deleting an item leaves its ref in\n`deleted_refs`, and a new ref is checked against both tables and that one.\n\nA site reference is resolved when a page is rendered (app.public_site), like\na chart image's `image:<name>`, so a link follows its target's slug, and only\na published target is linked.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport secrets\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Iterable\n\nfrom app import db\n\n# kind -> its table. The kind is also the site reference's scheme.\nTABLES = {\"data-bite\": \"data_bites\", \"report\": \"reports\"}\nREFERENCE = re.compile(r\"(data-bite|report):([0-9a-f]{32})\")\n# How many fresh refs to try before giving up.\n_ATTEMPTS = 3\n\n# What a site reference names, besides a published item: a draft, a deleted\n# item, or nothing that ever existed.\nPUBLISHED, DRAFT, DELETED, UNKNOWN = \"published\", \"draft\", \"deleted\", \"unknown\"\n\n\nclass RefCollision(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"Every fresh ref tried was taken: the generator is broken.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef reference(kind: str, ref: str) -> str:\n    return f\"{kind}:{ref}\"\n\n\ndef _generate() -> str:\n    return secrets.token_hex(16)\n\n\ndef _taken(conn: sqlite3.Connection, ref: str) -> bool:\n    return conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT 1 FROM data_bites WHERE ref = ?1 UNION ALL\"\n        \" SELECT 1 FROM reports WHERE ref = ?1 UNION ALL\"\n        \" SELECT 1 FROM deleted_refs WHERE ref = ?1\", (ref,)).fetchone() is not None\n\n\ndef new_ref(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A ref no item has, and no deleted item had. Run it in the\n    transaction that stores it, holding the write lock (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), so\n    that nothing else takes it in between. RefCollision after _ATTEMPTS.\"\"\"\n    for _ in range(_ATTEMPTS):\n        ref = _generate()\n        if not _taken(conn, ref):\n            return ref\n    raise RefCollision(f\"No unused ref after {_ATTEMPTS} attempts.\")\n\n\ndef tombstone(conn: sqlite3.Connection, kind: str, item_id: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Record the ref of the item about to be deleted, in the transaction\n    that deletes it.\"\"\"\n    conn.execute(f\"INSERT INTO deleted_refs (ref, kind) SELECT ref, ? FROM {TABLES[kind]}\"\n                 \" WHERE id = ? AND ref IS NOT NULL\", (kind, item_id))\n\n\ndef states(references: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"What each site reference names: PUBLISHED, DRAFT, DELETED, or\n    UNKNOWN (for anything not a well-formed one, too).\"\"\"\n    found = {}\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        for link in set(references):\n            match = REFERENCE.fullmatch(link)\n            if match is None:\n                found[link] = UNKNOWN\n                continue\n            kind, ref = match.groups()\n            row = conn.execute(f\"SELECT status FROM {TABLES[kind]} WHERE ref = ?\",\n                               (ref,)).fetchone()\n            if row is not None:\n                found[link] = PUBLISHED if row[\"status\"] == \"published\" else DRAFT\n            elif conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM deleted_refs WHERE ref = ? AND kind = ?\",\n                              (ref, kind)).fetchone():\n                found[link] = DELETED\n            else:\n                found[link] = UNKNOWN\n    return found\n\n\ndef state(link: str) -> str:\n    return states([link])[link]\n\n\ndef in_body(body: str) -> set[str]:\n    \"\"\"The site references a body names.\"\"\"\n    return {match[0] for match in REFERENCE.finditer(body or \"\")}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1774,"cache_read_input_tokens":149912,"output_tokens":2379,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":775},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1774,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2379,"cache_read_input_tokens":149912,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1774,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1774},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01USZS9Noth5wf8r8QfS6UQw":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/site_links.py","content":"\"\"\"Site links: a link in a body to another Data Bite or Report (spec #14,\n\"Links\").\n\nA link names its target by a *site reference*, `data-bite:<ref>` or\n`report:<ref>`, never by title, slug, or id: a title or slug may be edited,\nand SQLite may give a deleted item's id to a new one. Each item's `ref` is 32\nrandom hex characters, set when it is created and never changed (a trigger in\napp.db enforces it) or reused: deleting an item leaves its ref in\n`deleted_refs`, and a new ref is checked against both tables and that one.\n\nA site reference is resolved when a page is rendered (app.public_site), like\na chart image's `image:<name>`, so a link follows its target's slug, and only\na published target is linked.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport secrets\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Iterable\n\nfrom app import db\n\n# kind -> its table. The kind is also the site reference's scheme.\nTABLES = {\"data-bite\": \"data_bites\", \"report\": \"reports\"}\nREFERENCE = re.compile(r\"(data-bite|report):([0-9a-f]{32})\")\n# How many fresh refs to try before giving up.\n_ATTEMPTS = 3\n\n# What a site reference names, besides a published item: a draft, a deleted\n# item, or nothing that ever existed.\nPUBLISHED, DRAFT, DELETED, UNKNOWN = \"published\", \"draft\", \"deleted\", \"unknown\"\n\n\nclass RefCollision(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"Every fresh ref tried was taken: the generator is broken.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef reference(kind: str, ref: str) -> str:\n    return f\"{kind}:{ref}\"\n\n\ndef _generate() -> str:\n    return secrets.token_hex(16)\n\n\ndef _taken(conn: sqlite3.Connection, ref: str) -> bool:\n    return conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT 1 FROM data_bites WHERE ref = ?1 UNION ALL\"\n        \" SELECT 1 FROM reports WHERE ref = ?1 UNION ALL\"\n        \" SELECT 1 FROM deleted_refs WHERE ref = ?1\", (ref,)).fetchone() is not None\n\n\ndef new_ref(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A ref no item has, and no deleted item had. Run it in the\n    transaction that stores it, holding the write lock (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), so\n    that nothing else takes it in between. RefCollision after _ATTEMPTS.\"\"\"\n    for _ in range(_ATTEMPTS):\n        ref = _generate()\n        if not _taken(conn, ref):\n            return ref\n    raise RefCollision(f\"No unused ref after {_ATTEMPTS} attempts.\")\n\n\ndef tombstone(conn: sqlite3.Connection, kind: str, item_id: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Record the ref of the item about to be deleted, in the transaction\n    that deletes it.\"\"\"\n    conn.execute(f\"INSERT INTO deleted_refs (ref, kind) SELECT ref, ? FROM {TABLES[kind]}\"\n                 \" WHERE id = ? AND ref IS NOT NULL\", (kind, item_id))\n\n\ndef states(references: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"What each site reference names: PUBLISHED, DRAFT, DELETED, or\n    UNKNOWN (for anything not a well-formed one, too).\"\"\"\n    found = {}\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        for link in set(references):\n            match = REFERENCE.fullmatch(link)\n            if match is None:\n                found[link] = UNKNOWN\n                continue\n            kind, ref = match.groups()\n            row = conn.execute(f\"SELECT status FROM {TABLES[kind]} WHERE ref = ?\",\n                               (ref,)).fetchone()\n            if row is not None:\n                found[link] = PUBLISHED if row[\"status\"] == \"published\" else DRAFT\n            elif conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM deleted_refs WHERE ref = ? AND kind = ?\",\n                              (ref, kind)).fetchone():\n                found[link] = DELETED\n            else:\n                found[link] = UNKNOWN\n    return found\n\n\ndef state(link: str) -> str:\n    return states([link])[link]\n\n\ndef in_body(body: str) -> set[str]:\n    \"\"\"The site references a body names.\"\"\"\n    return {match[0] for match in REFERENCE.finditer(body or \"\")}\n"}},"serverClassifierRequest":"2279d03c-fc98-42a3-b9c0-98e324ddbd9d","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfaLGVb6Rh7xrSfZSdJ3J","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:tdd","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"236556da-b1d5-4034-b645-39286fb2f485","timestamp":"2026-09-30T21:28:01.315Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"5f1453e3-22ca-48ab-bcdf-08e3c322f1be","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"5fc2b53a-8927-4042-8fb2-5b6f5bbbd7d8","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaLQSsqvgRxyGkgdrkQS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_016ETYBnK5zqwT4RtJY9T2Rr","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t14_links.py","content":"\"\"\"T14: links to Reports and Data Bites, and the link rule (issue #17).\n\nA site link is stored as `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` and resolved\nwhen a page is rendered to the target's page-relative path, only if the\ntarget is published. Every other <a> keeps its href only as `https:` or\n`mailto:`; anything else, and a site link that doesn't resolve, renders as\nits text. Only `image:<name>` renders an <img>.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app import data_bites, public_site, reports\nfrom app.publish import render_site\nfrom tests.conftest import post_form\nfrom tests.test_t03_data_bites import create_bite\nfrom tests.test_t04_reports import create_report\nfrom tests.test_t07_public_site import crawl, published_bite, published_report\nfrom tests.test_t08_publish import exported\nfrom tests.test_t09_tables import content_body\nfrom tests.test_t12_site_preview import preview\n\nBITE_PAGE = \"/data-bites/fall-enrollment.html\"\n\n\ndef report_link(rid: str) -> str:\n    return f\"report:{reports.get(int(rid))['ref']}\"\n\n\ndef bite_link(bid: str) -> str:\n    return f\"data-bite:{data_bites.get(int(bid))['ref']}\"\n\n\ndef anchors(html: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Each <a>'s href in `html` (None for an <a> without one).\"\"\"\n    return [href or None for href in\n            (m[1] for m in re.finditer(r'<a\\b(?:[^>]*?\\bhref=\"([^\"]*)\")?[^>]*>', html))]\n\n\ndef linking_bite(c: TestClient, target: str, **override) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A published Data Bite at BITE_PAGE whose body links to `target`.\"\"\"\n    return published_bite(c, body=f\"See [the CDS]({target}) for more.\", **override)\n\n\ndef public_body(client: TestClient, path: str = BITE_PAGE) -> str:\n    return content_body(client.get(path).text)\n\n\n# Resolved site links\n\ndef test_a_link_to_a_published_report_is_page_relative(client_as, client, tmp_path):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    rid = published_report(director, slug=\"cds\", title=\"Common Data Set\")\n    linking_bite(director, report_link(rid))\n\n    assert anchors(public_body(client)) == [\"../reports/cds.html\"]\n    site = exported(render_site(tmp_path / \"site\"))\n    assert anchors(content_body(site[\"data-bites/fall-enrollment.html\"].decode())) == [\n        \"../reports/cds.html\"]\n    # crawl() follows it, so it reaches the page.\n    assert \"/reports/cds.html\" in crawl(client)\n\n\ndef test_a_link_to_a_published_data_bite_is_page_relative(client_as, client):\n    analyst = client_as(\"editor\")\n    target = published_bite(analyst, slug=\"spring-survey\", title=\"Spring survey\")\n    linking_bite(analyst, bite_link(target))\n    assert anchors(public_body(client)) == [\"spring-survey.html\"]\n\n\ndef test_a_link_follows_its_targets_slug(client_as, client):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    rid = published_report(director, slug=\"cds\", title=\"Common Data Set\")\n    linking_bite(director, report_link(rid))\n    post_form(director, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\",\n              {\"title\": \"Common Data Set 2026\", \"slug\": \"cds-2026\", \"body\": \"New.\"})\n    assert anchors(public_body(client)) == [\"../reports/cds-2026.html\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path, root\", [(\"index.html\", \"\"), site links in the Editor (issue #17): what the edit and create pages\ngive its link dialog's picker and markers, and what an Editor save keeps.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport re\nfrom html import unescape\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app import data_bites, reports\nfrom tests.conftest import post_form\nfrom tests.test_t03_data_bites import BITE, create_bite\nfrom tests.test_t04_reports import REPORT, create_report\nfrom tests.test_t07_public_site import published_bite, published_report\nfrom tests.test_t13_editor_routes import KINDS, edit_page, editor_content, save\nfrom tests.test_t14_links import bite_link, report_link\n\n\ndef data(page: str, name: str):\n    \"\"\"The Editor wrapper's `data-<name>` JSON.\"\"\"\n    [value] = re.findall(rf\"<div class=\\\"admin-editor\\\"[^>]*\\bdata-{name}='([^']*)'\", page)\n    return json.loads(unescape(value))\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef director(client_as):\n    return client_as(\"admin\")\n\n\ndef a_site(director: TestClient) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"A published and a draft Report and Data Bite, by name.\"\"\"\n    return {\"published report\": published_report(director, slug=\"cds\", title=\"Common Data Set\"),\n            \"draft report\": create_report(director, slug=\"draft-cds\", title=\"Draft CDS\"),\n            \"published bite\": published_bite(director, slug=\"spring\", title=\"Spring survey\"),\n            \"draft bite\": create_bite(director, slug=\"unreleased\", title=\"Unreleased count\")}\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", [\"/admin/data-bites\", \"/admin/reports\",\n                                  \"/admin/data-bites/{bite}\", \"/admin/reports/{report}\"])\ndef test_the_picker_lists_every_report_and_data_bite_marking_drafts(director, path):\n    site = a_site(director)\n    page = director.get(path.format(bite=site[\"draft bite\"],\n                                    report=site[\"draft report\"])).text\n    assert data(page, \"site-items\") == [\n        {\"href\": report_link(site[\"published report\"]), \"title\": \"Common Data Set\",\n         \"kind\": \"Report\", \"draft\": False},\n        {\"href\": report_link(site[\"draft report\"]), \"title\": \"Draft CDS\",\n         \"kind\": \"Report\", \"draft\": True},\n        {\"href\": bite_link(site[\"published bite\"]), \"title\": \"Spring survey\",\n         \"kind\": \"Data Bite\", \"draft\": False},\n        {\"href\": bite_link(site[\"draft bite\"]), \"title\": \"Unreleased count\",\n         \"kind\": \"Data Bite\", \"draft\": True},\n    ]\n\n\ndef test_the_picker_escapes_titles(director):\n    create_report(director, slug=\"x\", title=\"</div><script>alert(1)</script> 'q'\")\n    page = director.get(\"/admin/reports\").text\n    assert \"<script>alert(1)\" not in page\n    assert data(page, \"site-items\")[0][\"title\"] == \"</div><script>alert(1)</script> 'q'\"\n\n\ndef test_the_edit_page_names_each_unresolvable_links_state(director):\n    site = a_site(director)\n    doomed = create_report(director, slug=\"doomed\", title=\"Doomed\")\n    deleted = report_link(doomed)\n    assert post_form(director, f\"/admin/reports/{doomed}/delete\", {}).status_code == 303\n    unknown = \"data-bite:\" + \"e\" * 32\n    body = \" \".join(f\"[{n}]({link})\" for n, link in enumerate([\n        report_link(site[\"published report\"]), report_link(site[\"draft report\"]),\n        deleted, unknown]))\n    bid = create_bite(director, slug=\"linking\", {"parentUuid":"11b0f8d5-5e67-424f-b551-38ae84f91589","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0620594e-4d98-4377-a0b2-f29d0c1d1779","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review since 29a2cbb (T13 close). Originating ticket: GitHub issue #17 (T14: Links to Reports and Data Bites); spec: issue #14."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"2d898d78-aeb4-4685-adeb-1a742a788876","timestamp":"2026-09-30T21:41:39.215Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_011H6o7xnLK2MFPBYCH4ErbS","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"5f1453e3-22ca-48ab-bcdf-08e3c322f1be","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"b45d8d0c-9d5d-479a-9fe8-02ce4744a7b4","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0620594e-4d98-4377-a0b2-f29d0c1d1779","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015pHDy1JsrbnhFRiUJnYDn7","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n\n\ndef _load_dotenv(path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Read KEY=VALUE lines from .env into os.environ. Variables already set in\n    the real environment win.\"\"\"\n    if not path.is_file():\n        return\n    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():\n        key, sep, value = line.partition(\"=\")\n        key = key.strip()\n        if not sep or not key or key.startswith(\"#\"):\n            continue\n        os.environ.setdefault(key, value.strip().strip(\"'\\\"\"))\n\n\n_load_dotenv(ROOT / \".env\")\n\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSTATIC = ROOT / \"static\"  # the admin console's scripts, served under its login\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nSECRET_KEY_IS_PLACEHOLDER = SECRET_KEY in (\n    \"dev-only-not-for-production\", \"[REDACTED]\")\n# A relative CMS_DATABASE is relative to the repo, not the current directory.\nDATABASE_PATH = ROOT / os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", \"cms.db\")\n# Uploaded Report files. {"parentUuid":"b3f6c5d5-5792-4473-8c4e-90f160b98bfe","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0620594e-4d98-4377-a0b2-f29d0c1d1779","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Claude in Chrome browser automation\n\nYou have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.\n\n## Loading deferred tools\n\nIf the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:\n\nToolSearch with query \"select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp\"\n\nAdd task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.\n\n## GIF recording\n\nWhen performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.\n\nYou must ALWAYS:\n* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback\n* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., \"login_process.gif\")\n\n## Console log debugging\n\nYou can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: \"[MyApp]\" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.\n\n## Alerts and dialogs\n\nIMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:\n1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., \"Delete\" buttons with confirmation dialogs)\n2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session\n3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding\n\nIf you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.\n\n## Avoid rabbit holes and loops\n\nWhen using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:\n- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration\n- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts\n- No response from the browser extension\n- Page elements not responding to clicks or input\n- Pages not loading or timing out\n- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches\n\nExplain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.\n\n## Tab context and session startup\n\nIMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.\n\nNever reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:\n1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it\n2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp\n3. I found one test gap, some small unrequested behaviour, and one weak spot in how the delete list finds links.\n  \n  **(a) Missing or partial**\n  \n  1. **The id-reuse test doesn't check the \"Item deleted\" marker.** Spec: \"the **id-reuse** test (delete the target, create a new Report that may reuse its id, and the link is still plain text and \"Item deleted\")\". `test_a_link_to_a_deleted_report_never_reaches_a_new_one_with_its_id` (`tests/test_t14_links.py:124`) only checks the plain text. The `deleted` state is tested on its own in `test_the_edit_page_names_each_unresolvable_links_state`, but that test doesn't reuse the id. The code probably behaves correctly, because the new Report gets a different ref. The test just doesn't show it.\n  \n  2. **The Site preview is tested at one depth only.** Spec: \"a correct relative href at every depth, in the public site, the export, and the Site preview\". The every-depth test calls `Page` directly. The Site preview is tested once, for a Data Bite, and never for a Report preview. This is minor.\n  \n  **(b) Not asked for (scope creep)**\n  \n  1. **A database trigger blocks any change to a ref** (`app/db.py` `_REF_RULES`, `{table}_ref_fixed`). The spec asks for refs to be \"never changed by editing the title or slug\", not for a trigger. It's harmless, but it goes further than the spec.\n  2. **The Site preview links an item to itself** (`public_site._linked_as_published`). An item's own site links resolve as if it were already published. The spec doesn't mention this.\n  3. **Small Editor changes nobody asked for:**\n     - With no text selected, the new link's text is the item's title.\n     - Pressing Enter on a link-dialog button now presses that button.\n     - Changing the link dialog no longer counts as an unsaved change.\n  4. **The `CONTEXT.md` \"Site link\" glossary entry** is new. It is allowed by the CLAUDE.md glossary rule.\n  \n  **(c) Present but looks wrong**\n  \n  1. **The delete page can list items that don't really link.** Spec: \"Deleting an item lists the items whose bodies link to it\". `site_links.linked_from` runs `instr` plus the `REFERENCE` regex over the raw body. A reference in plain text or inside a code block counts as a link, so the page can list items that won't actually change. It will never miss a real link.\n  2. **A pasted link to a deleted item is marked \"Unknown link\", not \"Item deleted\".** Spec: the Editor marks \"Item deleted\" / \"Unknown link\". The deleted states (`data-link-states`) are worked out on the server, only for links in the saved body. `linkState` in `static/editor.js` treats any other unmatched ref as \"unknown\", until the page reloads. This is minor.\n  \n  **Checked and correct:**\n  - The `ref` column goes in through `ADDED_COLUMNS`, with backfill and a unique index.\n  - The tombstone is written in the same transaction as the delete.\n  - A new ref is checked under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` against both tables and `deleted_refs`, and `RefCollision` is raised after 3 attempts.\n  - The tombstoned-ref test is present.\n  - The picker lists items with drafts marked, and the external-link refusal message is there.\n  - The render-time rule applies to Markdown, raw HTML, and Editor saves.\n  - The absolute-image test in T10 was updated.\n  - The CLAUDE.md wording matches the spec exactly, and ADR-001 has its note.\n  - The crawler skips only `https:`/`mailto:` `<a href>`s, still fails on root-absolute paths, other schemes and absolute `src`, and has an injected-bad-URL test.\n</agent-message>"}

The report follows:\n  **Spec review: T14 (#17), diff 29a2cbb...HEAD**\n  \n  The 141 tests pass (the three T14 files plus T07 and T10). Almost every acceptance criterion is met. I found one test gap, some small unrequested behaviour, and one weak spot in how the delete list finds links.\n  \n  **(a) Missing or partial**\n  \n  1. **The id-reuse test doesn't check the \"Item deleted\" marker.** Spec: \"the **id-reuse** test (delete the target, create a new Report that may reuse its id, and the link is still plain text and \"Item deleted\")\". `test_a_link_to_a_deleted_report_never_reaches_a_new_one_with_its_id` (`tests/test_t14_links.py:124`) only checks the plain text. The `deleted` state is tested on its own in `test_the_edit_page_names_each_unresolvable_links_state`, but that test doesn't reuse the id. The code probably behaves correctly, because the new Report gets a different ref. The test just doesn't show it.\n  \n  2. **The Site preview is tested at one depth only.** Spec: \"a correct relative href at every depth, in the public site, the export, and the Site preview\". The every-depth test calls `Page` directly. The Site preview is tested once, for a Data Bite, and never for a Report preview. This is minor.\n  \n  **(b) Not asked for (scope creep)**\n  \n  1. **A database trigger blocks any change to a ref** (`app/db.py` `_REF_RULES`, `{table}_ref_fixed`). The spec asks for refs to be \"never changed by editing the title or slug\", not for a trigger. It's harmless, but it goes further than the spec.\n  2. **The Site preview links an item to itself** (`public_site._linked_as_published`). An item's own site links resolve as if it were already published. The spec doesn't mention this.\n  3. **Small Editor changes nobody asked for:**\n     - With no text selected, the new link's text is the item's title.\n     - Pressing Enter on a link-dialog button now presses that button.\n     - Changing the link dialog no longer counts as an unsaved change.\n  4. **The `CONTEXT.md` \"Site link\" glossary entry** is new. It is allowed by the CLAUDE.md glossary rule.\n  \n  **(c) Present but looks wrong**\n  \n  1. **The delete page can list items that don't really link.** Spec: \"Deleting an item lists the items whose bodies link to it\". `site_links.linked_from` runs `instr` plus the `REFERENCE` regex over the raw body. A reference in plain text or inside a code block counts as a link, so the page can list items that won't actually change. It will never miss a real link.\n  2. **A pasted link to a deleted item is marked \"Unknown link\", not \"Item deleted\".** Spec: the Editor marks \"Item deleted\" / \"Unknown link\". The deleted states (`data-link-states`) are worked out on the server, only for links in the saved body. `linkState` in `static/editor.js` treats any other unmatched ref as \"unknown\", until the page reloads. This is minor.\n  \n  **Checked and correct:**\n  - The `ref` column goes in through `ADDED_COLUMNS`, with backfill and a unique index.\n  - The tombstone is written in the same transaction as the delete.\n  - A new ref is checked under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` against both tables and `deleted_refs`, and `RefCollision` is raised after 3 attempts.\n  - The tombstoned-ref test is present.\n  - The picker lists items with drafts marked, and the external-link refusal message is there.\n  - The render-time rule applies to Markdown, raw HTML, and Editor saves.\n  - The absolute-image test in T10 was updated.\n  - The CLAUDE.md wording matches the spec exactly, and ADR-001 has its note.\n  - The crawler skips only `https:`/`mailto:` `<a href>`s, still fails on root-absolute paths, other schemes and absolute `src`, and has an injected-bad-URL test.\n</agent-message>","reason":"absorbed_mid_turn","commandUuid":"f5d4eecc-7334-492c-b7ca-69544d9057e6"}

{"parentUuid":"d36f70e7-aa87-4c89-a4c4-c5b5df650169","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaMdyUpjoy7vHtKK67eP","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'm stopping for one thing only you can do. T14 is built, reviewed, and committed in four commits. All 624 tests pass. What's left is the browser check, and I can't log in for it: the password field stays empty whether I fill it or type into it, so I won't try to get around that.\n\n**What I need:** in the Chrome tab I opened (http://127.0.0.1:8014/login), log in as `admin@example.test`. That server runs on a scratch database, not your `cms.db`. The password is the `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` value I seeded it with, `t14-browser-check-admin`. Then tell me you're in, and I'll do the rest:\n- the picker, with drafts marked\n- the refusal of an `http:` address\n- the three markers, on a seeded \"Link check\" Data Bite\n- screenshots at 1280, 768 and 390 wide\n\nAfter that I'll post the closing comment on #17 and make the `Closes #17` commit.\n\n**Commits**\n- `a4f24bd`: every Report and Data Bite gets a fixed `ref`, and deleting one records its ref so it's never reused. Pages link only to published items, with page-relative paths. This applies to the public site, the export, and the Site preview.\n- `7a5899a`: the Editor's link dialog has \"A page on this site\" and \"A web address\". The Delete button now opens a confirmation page listing the items that link to this one, as you chose.\n- `4e24d98`: the CLAUDE.md rule, a note in ADR-001, a \"Site link\" glossary entry, and the crawler change, with tests that inject bad URLs.\n- `bb22261`: fixes from the code review.\n\n**Changed behaviour you might notice**\n- **Existing content:** a link that isn't `https:`, `mailto:`, or a picked site link now shows as plain text. So does any image that isn't an uploaded chart image. The spec approved both. Two older T06/T10 tests asserted the opposite, and I updated them.\n- **Review fixes I made:**\n  - The site-link schemes are defined in one place.\n  - The two delete confirmations share one helper.\n  - ADR-005 now mentions site links.\n  - The deleted-then-reused-id test also checks the \"Item deleted\" marker.\n  - The Site preview test now covers Reports.\n- **Review findings I left as they are.** Each will go in the review comment on #17:\n  - The delete page finds linking items by searching body text. A reference typed as plain text would be listed too, but a real link is never missed.\n  - If you paste a link to a deleted item into the Editor, it says \"Unknown link\" until the page is reloaded.\n  - I added a small database trigger that stops a ref from ever changing. That goes slightly beyond the ticket.\n  - The picker label \"A page on this site\" uses \"page\", which the glossary lists under Report's _Avoid_ words. it names a place on the site, not a content type |\n| Confirm-delete `action` hard-coded beside a `url_path_for` | **Fixed**: the shared helper posts to its own path (`request.url.path`) |\n| Broken docstring line in `app/markdown_form.py` | **Fixed** |\n| Shotgun surgery: kind strings, schemes, and the reference pattern repeated | **Fixed**: `_URL_SCHEMES`, the Editor's posted schemes, and `REFERENCE` derive from `site_links.TABLES` (the JS keeps its own copy, as it has no server import) |\n| Primitive obsession: display noun used as a key | **Fixed**: `linked_from` returns `kind` and `noun`; the lookup is one dict read |\n| Speculative generality: `site_links.state()` only used by tests | **Kept**: it is the tests' seam onto `states()` |\n| Mysterious names (`found`, `keep`) | **Kept**: `found` is the existing idiom in `public_site`; `keep` reads as the filter's verb |\n\n### Spec\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| The id-reuse test didn't check \"Item deleted\" | **Fixed**: it also asserts the Editor's state for the old ref is `deleted` |\n| Site preview tested for Data Bites only | **Fixed**: parametrized over Data Bites and Reports |\n| Delete page lists by text match, so a reference typed as plain text would be listed too | **Kept**: it never misses a real link;
